attribution: Traditionally attributed to Dattatreya; author and date unknown
period: Date uncertain; often placed in the second millennium CE
summary: A song of the 'avadhuta', one who has shaken off all worldly and religious conventions, proclaiming the non-dual Self beyond all categories.
whyRead: The Avadhuta Gita expresses non-duality in ecstatic, sometimes paradoxical verse, denying even the categories of teacher, practice and liberation. It is valued in renunciant circles but is not an introductory text.
questions: What remains when all categories are dropped?
Can non-duality be spoken of at all?

keyTeachings.title: Everything is the Self
keyTeachings.text: The song repeatedly affirms that there is only the one Self, without division.

keyTeachings.title: Beyond all pairs
keyTeachings.text: It denies that the Self can be described as bound or free, pure or impure, one or many, since all such categories presuppose duality.

keyTeachings.title: The free renunciant
keyTeachings.text: The avadhuta is pictured as free of all social and ritual obligations, a figure for inner freedom.

structure.label: 8 chapters
structure.note: Scholars often regard the last chapter as a later addition

relatedTexts.note: Shares the negation of bondage and liberation from the highest standpoint
